thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — late-change window for Wed release train (slot #5, APAC-primary) opens in ~2h. If you have a must-ship change, post PR link + owner here. No late merges 30m before slot unless marshalled by release lead. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

aj: +1. My service has one tiny schema tweak (PR: github.com/redwood/svc/PR/412). Not risky, but will need a quick db-migration rollout. Owner: aj.

sam: Noted. Can you add a migration guard flag so we can roll back without downtime?

aj: Yep — migration is backwards-compatible + guard flag. Will mark the PR with "late-change" label and add smoke checklist.

maria: Thanks. @deploy-bot can you reserve slot #5 for the train and mark canary window at 2026-03-18T03:20Z?

deploy-bot: Reserved release-train slot #5 for Wed. Canary window: 2026-03-18T03:20Z–03:50Z UTC. Auto-notify: canary-owners.

jordan: SRE note — we'll need a canary traffic ramp: 1% → 10% over first 10m, health checks every 30s. If 5xx > 1% for 5m, auto-roll back. Also need migration index creation in off-peak shard only.

lee: I'll be oncall and smoke-owner for this slot. I'll do the smoke-run checklist and report within 10m of canary start.

maria: Perfect. Quick smoke checklist (we'll run these in order):
```
- deploy artifacts verified (sha match)
- service starts + no obvious OOMs
- /health returns 200 for primary routes
- perf sanity: p95 latency <= baseline + 50ms
- sample end-to-end flow: ingest -> model call -> store
- rollback test: dry-run rollback command verified
```

aj: For rollback, run: `infra deploy rollback svc-name --to-tag v2026.03.17-rc` — that runs a staged rollback and removes new migrations via guard flag. I'll keep the tag pinned.

sam: I'll add a quick smoke script under ops/smoke/slot5.sh that hits the main endpoints and validates token use. Will push before late-change window opens.

maria: Reminder: any late change must be approved by release lead (me) + oncall (lee) + service owner. If we get more than 2 late changes, we push to next train.

aj: ack. One question: if canary fails but fallback model-level variant exists, do we automatically route to the previous variant or do we failover to a cheaper model?

jordan: Routing policy for this train: prefer previous model variant in same region; fallback to cheaper model only if latency SLOs are breached and cost constraints are triggered. We'll capture exact traffic rules in the rollout notes.

lee: Also, quick ops note — keep a `kubectl get pods -n svc-name -o wide` handy and the command for rolling back CRDs: `kubectl apply -f crd-backup.yaml` if needed.

maria: If anyone expects to be offline during canary, call it out now. Otherwise we assume availability for quick rollback (<15m).

aj: I'll be available. Sam may be stepping out 10m into the window but reachable by phone.

sam: True — I'll be reachable by phone. If anything blocks, @maria escalate to next release lead.

maria: Cool. Final ask: drop PR links here once ready and prefix with [LATE] so QE knows to prioritize.

aj: PR: https://github.com/redwood/svc/pull/412 [LATE]

sam: Ops script PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/999 [LATE]

maria: Thanks. I'll close the late-change window 30m before the slot and post a final deploy roster. :white_check_mark:
